messages:
maya: quick summary from the shadow runs on prefill-only kv quant (fp8 vs int8) — posting raw numbers and a few hypotheses

maya: ran 10k inference requests against orion-13b canary yesterday, config: prefill enabled, kv-only quant (no weights quant), batch=1 seq=2048
maya: command used:
```
./shadow_runner --model=orion-13b --mode=shadow --kv-quant=INT8 --prefill=true --batch=1 --seq=2048 --reqs=10000
```

maya: raw aggregated results (INT8 vs FP8, kv-only)
memory: INT8 -> 28% lower GPU KV footprint vs FP8
throughput: INT8 ~ +6% tokens/s observed (warm)
latency (p50/p95/p99):
  FP8: 8.6ms / 21.3ms / 42.7ms
  INT8: 9.1ms / 22.0ms / 61.2ms  <-- notable p99 regression, ~18.5ms delta
cold-start prefill time (first token path):
  FP8 prefill: 120ms avg
  INT8 prefill: 260ms avg  <-- huge cold penalty for prefill in INT8 path
quality (LM evals on 2k prompts):
  small MAE drift (0.8% tokens changed), spot checks show occasional off-by-one on numeric sequences

ow: my hypothesis is that the INT8 path reduces per-KV memory but forces a slow dequant path on prefill that serializes operations and starves the async streamer, hence p99 spike and cold prefill latency. also eviction logic seems more aggressive because memory estimate rounding makes us hit eviction thresholds earlier.

ow pinging @owen and @sasha for kernel/dequant intuition
owen: yeah looks like the dequant op chain is the culprit. INT8 -> dequant -> matmul path currently uses a fallback kernel on cuda that doesn't fuse the prefill load + dequant + write-back. the FP8 path uses a fused kernel (thanks fp8 kernel team) so prefill writes are much faster.
owen: can you dump perf trace for a single cold prefill, maya? want nvtx + perf counters
maya: pasted perf trace gist: https://redwood-gists/internal/gh/1234 (shortened)

sasha: two quick suggestions: 1) try windowed prefill (prefill in 512-token slices) to let streaming overlap with dequant; 2) bump eviction margin by 10% in controller so INT8 has breathing room while we optimize kernels.
sasha: also: we saw earlier that INT8 rounding causes extra cache churn because allocations are slightly different sizes, so prefill touches different pages -> more TLB churn on some GPUs. worth checking big page alignment.

liam: bench-bot summary from the run:
bench-bot: shadow summary for 2955551234: requests=10000, avg_tokens_per_request=420, avg_lat=9.3ms, p99=61.2ms, gpu_mem_kv_fp8=4.2GB, gpu_mem_kv_int8=3.0GB, quality_regressions=0.8% (token-change), notes="INT8 prefill cold penalty high"

maya: thanks. suggestions for next steps:
- @owen try to prototype a fused dequant+write kernel or check if we can reuse fp8 kernel path for int8 when using same alignment
- @sasha flip eviction margin and run a short shadow with INT8 again (prefill full and windowed)
- @liam run an A/B shadow with hybrid kv: prefix FP8 + rest INT8 (split at 512 tokens) and collect p99 + mem + quality
- I'll prepare an eval set for arithmetic/token-stability to see where the 0.8% drift concentrates

owen: ok I'll dig into kernel plan. if we can fuse dequant + write we should recover most of the prefill penalty. worst case we add background async dequant thread to smooth p99.
sasha: will run two short shadows today: (A) INT8 with eviction_margin=+10% (B) hybrid split at 512 with windowed prefill=512. will tag results here.

liam: quick note on deployment profile: for Dedicated pools with strict latency SLOs we might prefer FP8 prefill for hot endpoints and INT8 for background long-lived sessions. hybrid seems like a good default. need to update console rollout logic to allow model-specific kv split flags.

maya: action items and owners pinned: 
- bench re-run (sasha): A/B by EOD -> post numbers
- kernel investigation (owen): prototype fused dequant plan by EOW
- hybrid shadow (liam): run split-prefill shadow, collect p99+mem+quality by mid-week
- eval set (maya): send arithmetic/length-sensitivity prompts to eng-evals by EOD

maya: anything else? otherwise I'll mark follow-ups in the tracker. :thumbsup:
liam: adding note: monitor eviction logs for 'size rounding' warnings, that will confirm the churn hypothesis.

a few quick inline snippets from nvprof for the cold prefill (INT8) that looked alarming:
```
GPU_0 prefill timeline:
  memcpy H2D  45ms
  dequant kernel  160ms
  write_kv  12ms
  total prefill 260ms
```

maya: ok closing for now, will post re-runs here. thanks all.
